newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FOCUS - First Austrian, Girocredit boost H1 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - First Austrian, Girocredit boost H1 profit.

text.p: First Austrian and GiroCredit banks, undertaking a merger to form Austria's second largest banking group, each reported moderately higher six-month earnings on Monday and forecast a stronger second half.

"It looks as though (First Austrian's) first-half figures will make up less than 50 percent of the full year," Andreas Treichl, chief executive of Die Erste Oesterreichische SparCasse-Bank (First Austrian), told reporters.
"GiroCredit has forecast a full-year operating profit of 1.5 billion schillings and it is very likely we will achieve that target," said Ferdinand Lacina, GiroCredit chief executive.

First Austrian said its parent operating profit edged 0.8 percent higher to 855 million schillings ($66 million) in the first six months. A 0.3 percent increase in operating income to 3.23 billion schillings outpaced a 0.1 percent rise in operating expenses to 2.37 billion.

GiroCredit posted a parent operating profit of 722 million schillings, a two percent rise. Its operating expenses fell three percent to 1.52 billion schillings, while operating income slipped one percent to 2.24 billion schillings.
First Austrian preferred shares were eight schillings up at 683 at midday. GiroCredit preferred were one down at 305.
Analysts said the results contained few surprises.
"It is too early to judge the merger between First Austrian and GiroCredit," said a London-based analyst.
The merger, which should be completed by the end of September and is effective January 1, 1997, will create a new group with assets of some 670 billion schillings.
First Austrian will account for 59 percent of the valuation of the new bank, while GiroCredit will account for 41 percent.
